coverage_of_risk.rationale: No tests of any kind exist in app/, so the riskiest logic (data transformation, URL state, pagination, sorting, error paths) is covered only by the slow, externally-owned acceptance suite.

regression_power.rationale: Nothing in app/ can fail. A refactor of the data layer would pass review and only be caught (if at all) by the harness's Playwright suite, which is not run as part of the app's own CI.

evidence: app/ — no spec/test files, so no padding or noise
tests/ — acceptance suite is external and not the agent's work
signal_to_noise.rationale: No tests means no low-value tests; neutral per the rubric, but the opportunity cost is high given how testable the logic is.

findings.issue: No test infrastructure at all: no test script, no vitest/@solidjs/testing-library dependency, no spec files in app/.
findings.suggestion: Add vitest + @solidjs/testing-library; start with unit tests for app/src/lib/util.ts and fixture-driven tests for toSpeciesCards and loadHomeData.

findings.issue: toSpeciesCards (alternate-form exclusion, dedupe, dual ref shapes, species-name mapping) is the core invariant of the whole app and is untested; idFromUrl (app/src/lib/util.ts:3-6) returns NaN for a non-numeric URL tail and NaN >= 10000 is false, so a malformed ref would render a card with sprite /media/sprites/pokemon/NaN.png.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test toSpeciesCards with mixed refs (learned_by_pokemon {name,url} vs type.pokemon {slot,pokemon}), duplicate refs, and a >=10000 form; assert NaN guards.

findings.issue: loadHomeData assembles per-species type slots via a sparse array indexed entry.slot-1 then filter(Boolean), and generation via a name->gen map where unmapped species silently become null (api.ts:79-84) and vanish from filtered views; a refactor here produces wrong counts and wrong type filters with no failing test.
findings.suggestion: Feed a small fixture JSON through loadHomeData (inject the fetcher) and assert the assembled species array, including a dual-slot, single-slot and unmapped-generation species.

findings.issue: Sort comparator: 'missing values sort last in both directions' depends on ma→1 ignoring dir; the classic refactor to (va - vb) * dir silently breaks null handling, and aria-sort toggling (line 266) is untested.
findings.suggestion: Extract the comparator into lib and unit-test both directions with nulls interleaved; component-test the header click cycle and aria-sort values.

findings.issue: Pagination clamp: /?page=999 renders the last page while the URL keeps page=999, so Previous/Next hrefs (index.tsx:140-144) disagree with the URL; page=abc falls back silently. Untested edge cases.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test the clamp/parse helpers (param('page') at index.tsx:23-28, pageHref at 60-68) for 0, negative, non-numeric and out-of-range values.

findings.issue: API failure handling: non-404 fetch errors throw through the 'use server' boundary with no ErrorBoundary in app/src/app.tsx:19, so an API 500 yields an unhandled rejection and a blank main; nothing tests the degraded path.
findings.suggestion: Add an ErrorBoundary around Suspense and a test that a 500 from a stubbed fetchApi renders a readable error instead of a blank page.

findings.issue: Hardcoded list limits (type/?limit=100, pokemon-species/?limit=3000, generation/?limit=100) silently truncate lists if the data ever grows past them; today's snapshot plus one overlay Pokémon passes, so no test would notice.
findings.suggestion: Either follow the `next` cursor, or add a test asserting the fetched count equals the reported API count.

findings.issue: Search debounce plus createEffect URL sync is the subtlest client code on the home page (rapid typing, back/forward, q cleared while typing) and is untested.
findings.suggestion: Component-test the input with clock-controlled debounce: URL updates ~150ms after typing, cleared search removes the q param, page resets.

findings.issue: Promise-cache failure eviction (p.catch(() => cache.delete(path))) has a real subtlety — an unhandled-rejection-shaped catch attached to a promise that is also returned to callers; concurrent rejections or a refactor to cache raw responses would change retry semantics untested.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test fetchApi: a 404 then a success (not cached), a 500 then recovery, and that in-flight promises are shared.

findings.issue: Game select silently falls back to the highest-order version group for an invalid ?game value, and MovesSection dedupes rows by method|level; both behaviours are untested.
findings.suggestion: Test that ?game=not-a-game selects the default and that the URL param is respected only for known games.

summary: The app contains no tests of its own — no runner, no script, no spec files — even though its riskiest logic (species/type/generation assembly, alternate-form filtering, pagination clamping, sort comparators) is pure or nearly pure and cheaply testable with vitest + @solidjs/testing-library. Everything is guarded only by the external Playwright acceptance suite, which is slow, harness-owned, and won't run in the app's own CI, so a data-layer refactor could regress counts, filtering and sorting with nothing failing locally. The code is otherwise clean and testable; adding a dozen focused unit/component tests would close most of the gap.

untested.area: Species/alternate-form mapping in toSpeciesCards and idFromUrl (app/src/lib/api.ts:70-90, app/src/lib/util.ts:3-6)
untested.likelyBug: A refactor to the ref parsing or the id>=10000 filter would include Mega forms in 'Learned by'/'Pokémon' lists and mislink cards to /pokemon/<pokemon name> instead of species names, and a NaN id would produce broken sprite URLs.

untested.area: Home data assembly: per-species type slots and generation mapping (app/src/lib/api.ts:94-136)
untested.likelyBug: Slot-ordered types would end up in the wrong order or missing (sparse-array filter), and species absent from generation lists would silently disappear from generation-filtered results while still counting toward 'N Pokémon'.

untested.area: Filtering, pagination math and URL state on / (app/src/routes/index.tsx:29-68)
untested.likelyBug: Off-by-one in slice bounds, page clamp disagreeing with the URL on ?page=999, or a filter change no longer resetting page to 1, each showing the wrong subset of species.

Method ordering (Level Up/Machine/Egg/Tutor then alphabetical) regressing to insertion order, null power/accuracy sorting first after a comparator 'simplification', or aria-sort never flipping to descending.

untested.area: API error and non-404 failure handling (app/src/lib/api.ts:13-24, app/src/app.tsx:19)
untested.likelyBug: An API 500 becomes an unhandled rejection past the 'use server' boundary, leaving a blank main landmark instead of an error state, and 404-vs-500 confusion could turn a missing resource into a crash instead of the Not found page.

untested.area: Latest English flavor text and English-name selection (app/src/lib/util.ts:18-29)
untested.likelyBug: Taking the first English entry instead of the last, or dropping the whitespace-collapse, would show stale, multi-line flavor text; falling back to any language would show French/Japanese text unnoticed.
Species or generations beyond the hardcoded limits are silently truncated, so new Pokémon would be missing from every list with no error.
Caching failures (including 404s) forever, or sharing rejected promises across concurrent requests, would make a transient API hiccup permanently poison a resource page until restart.
